title: Customer discovery and site assessment
audience: Any owner, sales contact or worker who speaks with a prospective customer before a job is booked in any service business.
learningOutcomes: Ask discovery questions that reveal the customer's needs, priorities, constraints and budget range.
Carry out a site assessment that identifies the scope, access, hazards and the surfaces involved.
Record the discovery and assessment so that the quote and the work order match the site.

instruction.heading: Discovery before the quote
instruction.body: Discovery is a short, structured conversation that finds out what the customer needs and why. Ask what they want done, what they have tried, what matters most to them, when they need it, who will be present, whether there are pets or children, and what they have already decided. Listen for needs the customer has not stated, such as a deadline or a guest arriving. Do not promise a result before you have seen the site. Record the answers in the customer record so that the next person can see them.

instruction.heading: Site assessment
instruction.body: A site assessment confirms the discovery by looking at the place. Note the size, the number of rooms or surfaces, the access and parking, the condition and finish of surfaces, the soil level, the presence of hazards such as wet floors, height, electrical items, unknown products or unsafe structures, and any restrictions on water, noise, waste or hours. Take photographs only with consent and under the privacy procedure. Record anything that changes the scope, the time or the method.

instruction.heading: Match scope to the site
instruction.body: Once the assessment is complete, check whether the customer's needs can be met safely and within the business's approved services. If the site needs a different method, a longer time or a referral, say so before the quote is issued. Record the assessment, the scope agreed and any item excluded. A quote built on a site visit is more accurate, and it protects the customer and the business from disputes later.

procedure: Ask the discovery questions and record the answers in the customer record.
Carry out the site assessment, noting size, access, surfaces, soil, hazards and restrictions.
Take photographs only with consent and within the privacy procedure.
Check that the needs can be met safely and within the approved services.
Record the scope agreed and any excluded item, and refer where needed.
Pass the assessment to the quote and work order so that they match the site.

workedExamples.situation: A customer on the phone wants a whole-house clean before a party on Saturday. On site you find a dog, a wet bathroom floor and heavy grease in the kitchen.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you record and do before quoting?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the dog, the wet floor hazard and the grease level as factors that change the time and method. Confirm whether the customer wants the grease removed, and quote for the agreed scope only. State any excluded item and the time the job will take, then pass the assessment to the quote.

equipmentAndPpe: Camera or phone for consented photographs only

commonErrors.prevention: Assess the site before a firm quote where the work is not standard.

commonErrors.error: Promising outcomes such as 'it will look brand new'.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the agreed scope and the standard, not the outcome.

commonErrors.error: Taking photographs of personal items during the assessment.
commonErrors.prevention: Photograph only with consent and only what the assessment needs.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Site hazards found during assessment must be recorded and managed before the job, and a job that cannot be done safely must be declined or referred. This lesson does not grant any licence or authority to carry out the work.

qualityStandard: Discovery answers are recorded before the quote is issued.
Each site assessment records size, access, surfaces, soil, hazards and restrictions.
The scope agreed matches the assessment, with exclusions stated.
documentationEvidence: Discovery record with the customer's needs, priorities and constraints.
Site assessment record with the findings, photographs taken with consent, and the scope agreed.
summary: Ask structured discovery questions and record the answers.
Assess the site for scope, access, surfaces, soil, hazards and restrictions.
Quote only for the scope the site and the approved services support.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a site assessment do before a firm quote?
options: Nothing; the phone call is enough and the customer has agreed to it.
Promise the customer a result by the end of the next working week.
Confirm the scope, access, surfaces, hazards and restrictions on site.

knowledgeChecks.question: On site you find a hazard that the customer did not mention. What is correct?
options: Record it, check whether the job can be done safely, and adjust the scope or refer before quoting.
Quote the job as is, and deal with the hazard later if it arises and note it on the form.
Start the job and deal with it later once the work is under way and the customer has paid for the day.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of these does the discovery conversation ask about?
options: Whether there are pets or children
